steps.title: A workspace, an ontology, and the people who may use it
steps.story: Every workspace starts with a published ontology (the schema for what can be known) and registered principals. A trusted conversation app, a Research agent, a Planning agent and an agent with no grants are registered, each with its own key and its own grants.
steps.look_for: The ontology version and content hash, and that each principal gets a key shown exactly once.

steps.title: Facts that come from systems are commands, not guesses
steps.story: The HR system's facts (Sarah works at Acme, first as an engineer, then as a manager) go in as deterministic commands. They are projected into the graph with zero model calls, and sending the same Idempotency-Key twice is one logical write.
steps.look_for: model_calls is 0, and the repeated request returns the same entity.

steps.title: A conversation is processed through the model pipeline
steps.story: Sarah says she is "considering entrepreneurship" and mentions Michael. This one goes through the full pipeline: normalise, extract entities and facts, resolve identities, write curated memory. The interaction record shows each stage.
steps.look_for: The stage list reaching "indexed" - this is the write path the Write path page animates.

request.content: Sarah Johnson: I'm considering entrepreneurship, and Michael, who I've known for years, keeps encouraging me.

steps.title: Verified facts and unverified claims stay separate
steps.story: Sarah currently works at Acme as an Engineering Manager, a verified fact from the HR system. "Considering entrepreneurship" is a separate, unverified conversation report, and an episodic memory records the conversation itself.
steps.look_for: evidence_status verified versus unverified, and authority_class authoritative_system versus conversation_report.

items.summary: Sarah is considering entrepreneurship: a possible software business

steps.title: The Research agent publishes a sourced finding, keeps a private note
steps.story: The Research agent reads context, ingests its source document, saves a private working note, and proposes a project-scoped finding that cites the document. The finding becomes active and shared; the note stays private to the agent.
steps.look_for: The finding's status "active" with its source event, and the working note that no other agent will ever see.

steps.title: The Planning agent gets a bounded, cited context
steps.story: The Planning agent asks for context for a task at a 600-token budget. It gets current facts, the shared finding, the open question ("how long is the runway?") as an explicit unknown, and citations. The cycling distractor and the research agent's private note are absent.
steps.look_for: used_tokens within the budget, the unknowns list, citations, and that nothing off-topic made it in.

steps.title: Outsiders learn nothing
steps.story: An agent from another workspace, and an agent with no grants, ask about Sarah. A hidden entity returns exactly the same 404 as one that never existed, and the context comes back "denied" or empty. Nothing about Sarah leaks, not even that she exists.
steps.look_for: Byte-identical 404 bodies for a real and a made-up id.

steps.title: A wrong extraction is rejected and disappears
steps.story: The model extracted "Michael manages Sarah" from a message. It is labelled unverified in context, a reviewer rejects it with a reason, and the next context no longer contains it. The original message stays on record.
steps.look_for: The MANAGES fact in the first context, absent in the second; the interaction still retrievable.

steps.title: Deleting a person, with a receipt
steps.story: A deletion request for Michael blocks reads immediately, then a purge removes his data from the ledger, the graph, the vector index and traces. A receipt proves what was removed and that no identifiers remain.
steps.look_for: The 404 right after the request, then a receipt listing each store and zero residual ids.

steps.title: When the model is down, nothing is lost
steps.story: With the model provider failing, a new event is accepted and queued. Context keeps serving what the ledger already holds. After the fault clears, replaying the event completes the pipeline.
steps.look_for: processing_status "processing" during the outage, context still "complete", then "indexed" after replay.
